description: QA Test Plan v2 — BatchExporter (Blender 4.0+ Extension)
notes: Excludes 27 tests that passed clean in v1. Retains fixed-bug re-verification, updated-behaviour checks, and new-feature tests.

categories.title: Bug Fix Re-verification
categories.description: Tests that failed in v1 and were fixed. Must be re-run to confirm the fixes.

tests.title: Export by Scenes — View Layer Fix
tests.bug_fixed: Objects in other scenes caused RuntimeError when not in the active view layer. Fixed by filtering to view_layer_objects before selecting.
steps: Create 2 scenes, each with at least 1 mesh object
Switch to Scene 1
Open Batch Export, set scope to 'Scenes'
Set output dir, format to FBX, click OK
expected: One .fbx file per scene, named after the scene
No RuntimeError about view layer
Each file contains the meshes from that scene
Info area shows correct succeeded count

tests.title: Export All Objects — View Layer Fix
tests.bug_fixed: Iterating bpy.data.objects included objects from all scenes/excluded layers. Fixed to iterate bpy.context.view_layer.objects instead.
steps: Create a scene with 4 mesh objects visible in the current view layer
Optionally add objects to other scenes or hide some from the view layer
Open Batch Export, set scope to 'All Objects'
Set output dir, format to FBX, click OK
expected: Only objects in the current view layer are exported
Four individual .fbx files created for visible objects
Non-mesh objects (cameras, lights) are excluded
No RuntimeError about view layer objects

tests.title: Export as OBJ — Operator Fix
tests.bug_fixed: Blender 4.0+ replaced export_scene.obj with wm.obj_export. Fixed operator ID and kwargs (export_selected_objects instead of use_selection).
steps: Select 1 mesh object
Set format to OBJ
Export
expected: A valid .obj file is created
No 'operator not found' error in the console
File can be re-imported into Blender

tests.title: Invalid Output Path — Graceful Error
tests.bug_fixed: pathlib.mkdir() threw unhandled FileNotFoundError for non-existent drives (e.g. Z:\). Fixed with try/except wrapping, re-raises as OSError with descriptive message.
steps: Set output directory to a non-existent drive or invalid path (e.g. 'Z:\nonexistent\path')
Select an object and attempt to export
expected: Export fails gracefully with a descriptive error in the report
Error message includes 'Cannot create' and the offending path
Report shows 0 succeeded, 1+ failed with error details
Blender remains usable (no crash)

categories.title: Updated Behaviour Checks
categories.description: Tests whose expected behaviour changed due to UX improvements. Must be re-run with updated expectations.

tests.title: Counter Digits Start at 1
tests.origin: v1 test 4.4 (PASSED with note — counter started at 0)
tests.change: Counter now starts at 1 instead of 0. enumerate(items, start=1).
steps: Select 3 mesh objects
Expand Naming, set Counter Digits to 3
Export as FBX with scope='Selected Objects'
expected: Files have 1-based zero-padded counters: e.g. 'Cube_001.fbx', 'Sphere_002.fbx', 'Cylinder_003.fbx'
Counter does NOT start at 000

tests.title: Scope-aware Empty Selection Message
tests.origin: v1 test 7.2 (PASSED with note — message was generic)
tests.change: Message is now scope-aware: 'No objects selected.' for SELECTED scope, 'Nothing to export for the selected scope.' for others.
steps: Deselect all objects (Alt+A)
Open Batch Export, set scope to 'Selected Objects'
Set a valid output directory, click OK
Then change scope to 'All Objects' with an empty scene and repeat
expected: With 'Selected Objects' scope: Warning says 'No objects selected.'
With other scopes (empty scene): Warning says 'Nothing to export for the selected scope.'
No files created, no crash

tests.title: Filename Preview Shows Counter Starting at 1
tests.origin: v1 test 2.3 (PASSED — but preview counter updated)
tests.change: Preview counter context changed from '0' to '1'.
steps: Open the Batch Export dialog
Expand Naming, set Counter Digits to 3
Observe the preview filename
expected: Preview shows counter as '001' (not '000')
e.g. 'ObjectName_001.fbx'

categories.title: New Feature — Advanced UI Section
categories.description: A new collapsible 'Advanced' section was added to the popup dialog.

tests.title: Advanced Section Visible and Collapsible
steps: Open the Batch Export dialog
Observe the layout — there should be four sections: Output, Naming, Filters, Advanced
Click the 'Advanced' triangle to expand it
Verify all advanced options appear
Click the triangle again to collapse
expected: Advanced section is collapsed by default (triangle points right)
Expanding shows three checkboxes: 'Export at Origin', 'Pack LODs', 'Export Textures'
Collapsing hides all three options
Triangle icon toggles between TRIA_RIGHT and TRIA_DOWN

categories.title: New Feature — Export at Origin
categories.description: Temporarily moves objects to world origin (0,0,0) during export, then restores positions.

tests.title: Export at Origin — Objects Moved to Origin
steps: Place a mesh object at location (5, 10, 3)
Select it, open Batch Export
Expand Advanced, enable 'Export at Origin'
Export as FBX
expected: A valid .fbx file is created
Re-importing the FBX shows the object at world origin (0, 0, 0)
The original object in the scene is back at (5, 10, 3) after export

tests.title: Export at Origin — Disabled by Default
steps: Place a mesh object at location (5, 10, 3)
Select it, export with default Advanced settings (Export at Origin unchecked)
expected: Re-importing the FBX shows the object at its original location (5, 10, 3)
Position is NOT reset to origin

tests.title: Export at Origin — Multiple Objects
steps: Place 3 mesh objects at different locations: (1,2,3), (4,5,6), (7,8,9)
Select all 3, enable 'Export at Origin'
Export as FBX with scope 'Selected Objects'
expected: Three .fbx files created
Each file has its object at (0, 0, 0) when re-imported
All original objects are restored to their original positions after export

tests.title: Export at Origin — Restores on Failure
steps: Place an object at (5, 10, 3)
Enable 'Export at Origin'
Set output to an invalid path to force an export error
expected: Export fails with a graceful error
The object's location is restored to (5, 10, 3) even after failure

categories.title: New Feature — LOD Packing
categories.description: Groups LOD variants (e.g. Cube_LOD0, Cube_LOD1) into a single export file.

tests.title: LOD Packing — Groups LOD Variants
steps: Create 4 objects: 'Chair_LOD0', 'Chair_LOD1', 'Table_LOD0', 'Table_LOD1'
Select all 4, open Batch Export
Expand Advanced, enable 'Pack LODs'
Export as FBX with scope 'Selected Objects'
expected: Two .fbx files created: 'Chair.fbx' and 'Table.fbx'
Chair.fbx contains both Chair_LOD0 and Chair_LOD1 meshes
Table.fbx contains both Table_LOD0 and Table_LOD1 meshes
Report shows 2 succeeded

tests.title: LOD Packing — Mixed LOD and Non-LOD Objects
steps: Create 3 objects: 'Chair_LOD0', 'Chair_LOD1', 'Lamp'
Select all 3, enable 'Pack LODs'
Export as FBX
expected: Two .fbx files: 'Chair.fbx' (packed LODs) and 'Lamp.fbx' (standalone)
Report shows 2 succeeded

tests.title: LOD Packing — Disabled by Default
steps: Create 2 objects: 'Chair_LOD0', 'Chair_LOD1'
Select both, leave 'Pack LODs' unchecked
Export as FBX
expected: Two separate .fbx files: 'Chair_LOD0.fbx' and 'Chair_LOD1.fbx'
Objects are NOT grouped

tests.title: LOD Pattern Recognition
steps: Create objects with various LOD naming patterns: 'Cube_LOD0', 'Cube-LOD1', 'CubeLOD2', 'Cube_lod3'
Select all, enable 'Pack LODs', export
expected: All four objects are grouped into a single 'Cube.fbx' file
The regex pattern handles underscore, hyphen, and no separator, and is case-insensitive

categories.title: New Feature — Texture Export
categories.description: Copies textures used by exported objects into a subfolder per material alongside the exported files.

tests.title: Texture Export — Copies Textures
steps: Create a mesh object with a material that has an Image Texture node pointing to a valid image file
Select it, expand Advanced, enable 'Export Textures'
Export as FBX
expected: The .fbx file is created
A 'textures/<MaterialName>/' folder is created in the output directory
The image file is copied into that folder
Info area shows 'Copied N texture(s).'

tests.title: Texture Export — Skips Duplicates
steps: Create 2 objects sharing the same material with the same image texture
Select both, enable 'Export Textures'
Export
expected: The texture file is copied only once (no duplicate copies)
Info shows 'Copied 1 texture(s).' (not 2)

tests.title: Texture Export — No Textures Graceful
steps: Create an object with a material that has no Image Texture nodes
Enable 'Export Textures', export
expected: Export succeeds normally
No 'textures/' folder is created
No error or crash

tests.title: Texture Export — Disabled by Default
steps: Create an object with image textures
Leave 'Export Textures' unchecked, export
expected: No 'textures/' folder is created
No textures are copied

tests.title: Texture Export — Missing Source File
steps: Create a material with an Image Texture node, but point it to a file that doesn't exist on disk
Enable 'Export Textures', export
expected: The export itself succeeds
The missing texture is silently skipped (no crash, no error)
Other valid textures are still copied

categories.title: New Feature — Progress Indicator
categories.description: Uses Blender's window manager progress API to show export progress in the status bar.

tests.title: Progress Bar During Export
steps: Create a scene with 10+ mesh objects
Select all, export as FBX
Watch the Blender status bar during export
expected: A progress indicator is visible in the Blender status bar during export
Progress advances as each item is exported
Progress bar disappears after export completes

tests.title: Progress Cleans Up on Failure
steps: Set up a scenario where export partially fails mid-way
Observe the progress bar after the export finishes
expected: wm.progress_end() is called even if some exports fail
No stuck progress indicator in the status bar
